Published September 30, within the authoritative window. Useful original researcher account of reward design and human-gated experimental automation. 'A better PLM recipe' reports contact precision rising from 28.2% to 36.6% P@L at 48.4B tokens; this is an author-reported relative improvement of about 30%, not 30 percentage points or evidence of fully autonomous discovery. 'Failure mode' reports two 72-round searches improving validation loss without matching the best contact precision, directly motivating scrutiny of proxy rewards. 'What survived the human gate' describes two seeds, a noise-aware retention rule and four of seven changes surviving scaled-up ablation. These concrete campaign details provide the new evidence and practical lessons for student experiment design. Limitations: the supplied blog lacks numerical ablation tables, hardware, total search cost, execution logs and independent replication; equal token budgets alone do not establish equal compute cost, and contact precision remains a proxy. The authors describe their own project and promote its adoption; no financial conflict is disclosed in the supplied text. Its referenced paper is the same underlying work, not independent corroboration, and workshop status is not validation. Published October 7, within the authoritative window. Strong fit for all three pieces: the new evidence combines agent-written kernel components, trusted assembly, frozen validation selection, held-out families and matched search ablations. Appendix A.6 reports failures among numerically screened unrestricted programs of 12/35, 18/31 and 8/37; these support scrutiny of finite tests, not a universal failure rate. Preserve the qualification in Proposition 1 and Appendix A.1: kernel validity assumes finite, correctly shaped, pure components; sampled conformance tests do not prove purity throughout the domain. Appendices B.5–B.7 distinguish ablation campaigns from headline campaigns and show important limits: broader frozen DWF prediction wins only 44/88 synthetic comparisons and 4/16 real-data comparisons. Appendix D.3 attributes much forecasting advantage to reversed windows and reports stronger CAKE results at the ten-year forward horizon. Appendix E.2 uses simulated patients, and none of its 35 nMSE contrasts survives the stated Holm correction. These findings constrain broad superiority claims rather than being averaged away. For students, the inference is to separate proposal, verification and selection and test beyond the discovery distribution. Appendix D.1 provides calls, tokens and timing, but not a complete hardware/dollar budget. This is an author-run preprint without supplied independent replication; author affiliations and financial conflicts remain unresolved. Some code/prompt listings are absent from the supplied extraction, limiting reproducibility claims. October 5 publication is within the authoritative window; October 7 update and October 15 retrieval are separate metadata events. The substantive novelty is agent-edited molecular optimizers searched using inexpensive xTB evaluations and tested on unseen molecules and potentials. Authors report AutoSella-F using 40.24–77.20% of Sella's per-molecule DFT force calls across four datasets ([saved text, §4.2 and Table 2](data/assets/27b20d8820941053973c26f4/4126f2eebaafaa9fde65cc866a5d982ad2139e084a6753ba820a51c5aa797b72/text.txt)). This supports a practical series example of protected evaluation, candidate provenance and surrogate-to-target testing. Evidence includes 27 baseline configurations, two 66-hour main searches, 192 CPU workers, conditional component ablations and a supplied code-release link; these do not establish independent replication or student-scale affordability ([saved text, §3.4 and Appendices C, F–G](data/assets/27b20d8820941053973c26f4/4126f2eebaafaa9fde65cc866a5d982ad2139e084a6753ba820a51c5aa797b72/text.txt)). Qualify the abstract's claim that both variants improve consistently: AutoSella-A regresses on solvated systems, including 109.06% of baseline DFT calls with lower mean energy recovery. Means exclude unsuccessful paired optimizations; force-call savings are not measured total monetary savings. Average energy recovery also does not guarantee the same minimum or protect every molecule: AutoSella-F meets the same-minimum criterion on only 1% of solvated systems under xTB ([saved text, Tables 1–2 and Appendices D–E](data/assets/27b20d8820941053973c26f4/4126f2eebaafaa9fde65cc866a5d982ad2139e084a6753ba820a51c5aa797b72/text.txt)). Repeated validation feedback is selection evidence, not untouched final-test evidence; ablation contributions are nonadditive, and search and final comparisons use different fragment settings ([saved text, §3.4 and Appendices B, G.4](data/assets/27b20d8820941053973c26f4/4126f2eebaafaa9fde65cc866a5d982ad2139e084a6753ba820a51c5aa797b72/text.txt)). Retain the poor Grok run as a boundary case, not a general model ranking (Appendix H). This is author-reported preprint evidence with extensive disclosed AI assistance; no independent researcher assessment or financial-conflict disclosure is supplied. Student takeaway: copy the separation of search and final evaluation, and inspect failures and per-instance quality alongside aggregate gains.

Published October 1 within the authoritative window. Offers concrete new evidence about separating research allocation from execution, preserving experiment records, and training decision policies. Distinguish frozen-weight MIRA orchestration from MIRA-AC's actual LoRA weight updates; neither should be described merely as improved instructions ([saved text, §§3.3, 6.1 and Appendix H](data/assets/2c2f305856a15081f2fe9066/2c18cdc1f7cd0b9f4f773d6fa5733d29d115f5752e8ad9fe28d99ad61680389e/text.txt)). Useful controls include output-token-matched theorem-proving continuations, proxy versus gold evaluation, and an ablation ladder. Token matching recovers most of the theorem-proving gap, limiting attribution to orchestration alone ([saved text, §§6.1–6.3](data/assets/2c2f305856a15081f2fe9066/2c18cdc1f7cd0b9f4f773d6fa5733d29d115f5752e8ad9fe28d99ad61680389e/text.txt)). Preserve heterogeneous results: environment-specific proxy MIRA-AC solves 48 BNLearn tasks versus untrained MIRA's 76, while the cross-environment policy solves 84. BNLearn was excluded from actor training but included in critic pretraining; this is not wholly unseen-environment transfer. Scientific-task training and evaluation reuse task identities and seeds, and only one policy is trained per configuration ([saved text, §6.3 table and Appendices B.1, H](data/assets/2c2f305856a15081f2fe9066/2c18cdc1f7cd0b9f4f773d6fa5733d29d115f5752e8ad9fe28d99ad61680389e/text.txt)). Shared-parameter comparisons also change initialization and adapter configuration; behavioral explanations rely on LLM judgments, with unequal forced continuation in symbolic regression. Neither establishes the causal value of a specific research habit ([saved text, §6.3, Appendix H and K.4](data/assets/2c2f305856a15081f2fe9066/2c18cdc1f7cd0b9f4f773d6fa5733d29d115f5752e8ad9fe28d99ad61680389e/text.txt)). The general training setup uses 32 H200s, and context-cost savings are replay projections with omitted costs, not measured end-to-end savings (Appendix H). Students can adapt bounded work orders, persistent failure records and sealed final evaluation without assuming affordable retraining or universal gains (Appendix C). Treat as one team's preprint, not independent corroboration of the other papers; independent replication and practitioner assessment are absent. A Meta-domain author contact appears in the supplied header, but funding and financial conflicts remain undisclosed in the supplied evidence.

The supplied publication date, October 13, falls within September 16–October 15. Accept as a new, bounded evaluation of claim completion, not a general ranking of research agents. The saved full text reports 14/90 end-to-end claims met, with only one empirical claim met; Appendix G, Table 16 and its following example distinguish reported success from adequate baselines, calibration tests and latency measurements. These support practical student advice to freeze criteria and audit artifacts ([saved text](data/assets/51fd6c05fff2f297f454f717/9f5a3d8ad0d87cf4b75e0b27ee825183acc71c2811e8bb96e1a59f3c5dca2c35/text.txt), Appendix G). Limits are substantial: one anchor-paper task; an LLM judge with researcher spot-checking rather than demonstrated independent replication; reference-dependent scoring that rewards expected positive outcomes; and possible pretraining exposure (§§3.3, 4.1, 6; Appendix E). Test sessions could inform optimization, so these are not untouched held-out estimates (Appendix B, 'Data and test access'). September 16 is inside the inclusive window. The new publication reports an older April 26–May 8 experiment; present the report and its provenance analysis as new evidence, not a newly occurring run. Accept for its concrete Git-based experiment lineage, negative-result records and verification design ([saved text](data/assets/59b2cb8b434efeeb70a133bc/66025228eaffdbf60602a9c3e085782385578f7304cce9751aff2a52b9936729/text.txt), §§3.2, 4.3–4.5). The authors report a development-score reduction from 3.3923 to 1.899044 bpb, but every component was selected on the same 200 texts; this is not held-out generalization. About 98% of the reduction came from the first 18 scored contributions, and the final improvement was below cross-hardware variation (§4.5, 'Trajectory' and 'Primary result'). The 165 verifications are other-account checks within one project, not independent research-team replication; one confirmation exceeded the stated approximate tolerance (§4.5, 'Lineage and reproduction'). Missing evaluator logs and dependency/data pins, plus the authors' explicit statement that they did not rerun the winner, limit reproducibility (§4.8). Human prompt and server changes, manual sessions, shared process visibility and mutable index records qualify claims of autonomous coordination (§§4.2, 4.7). Each worker had an 80-GB GPU, but no matched efficiency comparison establishes compute savings (§4.2; conclusion). Students can adopt provenance and failure logging without assuming this scale or performance transfers. The platform builders report their own experiment, creating an evaluative interest; financial conflicts are unspecified. Retain these caveats rather than treating account counts as corroborating independent sources.

The September 24 publication is in-window; it reports a preceding twelve-week campaign rather than dating every experiment to this window. Accept as a practitioner case study of costly failures, persistent memory and metric design, with performance claims attributed to the authors. Concrete examples include eleven consecutive evaluation timeouts, repeated failed configurations and coherence gains obtained through unusable singleton clusters ([saved text](data/assets/7082835cef4c8540dcb8d480/7d04403761d8cb23614022d48ddb879a6de4fb7f5af821bb1d1d2cb773d97ec4/text.txt), §§III-A–III-E). These make cost-sensitive checks and human evaluation design relevant to smaller student experiments; the authors themselves call the cost principle a two-data-point observation (§VI). Report the 1.82× Recall@6 lift as a peak: the across-date mean is 6.18%, or 1.63× the hand-tuned baseline, across eleven dates; these remain offline proxies (§§V-A, V-E). Examine two internal tensions explicitly: §V-E says an immutable evaluator prevents metric gaming, yet §III-E documents gaming without evaluator edits; §V-A claims agent additions establish causality, while §VI admits observational transitions cannot exclude accumulated search. Neither unsuccessful search nor unmet usability targets proves an inherent tradeoff. System B used human pivots and one researcher agent, so its gain does not independently validate the three-agent framework (§IV, Table III; §V-C). Proprietary purchase data and unavailable underlying experiment records prevent independent verification of numerical gains; no independent replication or online outcome validation is supplied (Reproducibility; §VI, 'Limitations'). Accept the inspectable methodological account, not established efficacy. This is an Amazon deployment account using Amazon Bedrock, with an organizational commercial interest; two internal workstreams are not independent external corroboration (§I; Acknowledgment).

The supplied September 30 publication date falls within September 16–October 15. Accept as a new controlled comparison useful for choosing student experiment baselines, not proof that harnesses never help. The authors report matched backbones, hardware and budgets; GLM 5.2 self-selected medal rates are 62.5% for Malena versus 47.1% for AiScientist ([saved text, §3 and D.2, Tables 15–16](data/assets/7f0901064878a294934bd154/6c598d9a3db4f487a0045a147e48bc3e4064e2b81bf388f4ac0947b9d96c78ec/text.txt#:~:text=D.2%20Detailed%20MLE-bench%20results)). Preserve exceptions: Gemma significantly favors MLEvolve on percentile, and failure to detect a difference does not establish equivalence. Ablations use original default29 tasks, whereas external comparisons use repaired fixed30 tasks; NatureBench permits unlimited evaluation queries and reports oracle best scores, so it is not an independent untouched-test confirmation ([A.1–A.3 and D.6](data/assets/7f0901064878a294934bd154/6c598d9a3db4f487a0045a147e48bc3e4064e2b81bf388f4ac0947b9d96c78ec/text.txt#:~:text=D.6%20NatureBench)). Cost claims require separation of the experiment worker from eight-GPU backbone hosting and modeled cache charges; minimal architecture does not mean cheapest inference ([A.4 and §5.1](data/assets/7f0901064878a294934bd154/6c598d9a3db4f487a0045a147e48bc3e4064e2b81bf388f4ac0947b9d96c78ec/text.txt#:~:text=A.4%20LLM%20backbones%20used)). The preprint supplies implementation details and repair diffs, but no independent replication is supplied. The affiliation header identifies EPFL/Apple and Apple internship work; authors evaluate their own system and acknowledge tuning asymmetry, contamination risk and only 3–4 seeds for 24-hour runs ([G.1](data/assets/7f0901064878a294934bd154/6c598d9a3db4f487a0045a147e48bc3e4064e2b81bf388f4ac0947b9d96c78ec/text.txt#:~:text=G.1%20Limitations)). Editorial implication: start with a simple baseline, protect evaluation data and measure total cost before adding orchestration.

The supplied October 8 publication date is eligible. Accept as new evidence about prioritizing experiments using recorded outcomes, with practical relevance to preserving failed runs and testing selection policies. The authors report 2,653 experimental records, held-out intervention forecasts, kNN/ridge controls and exclusion of near-duplicate intervention groups in cross-environment histories ([§3.1–3.2](data/assets/813b9149789f0913c5bfb94d/4e9fb103fdae9cf7e73a08394a425933da944a26fb69499d2c2935840571b3d8/text.txt#:~:text=3.1%20Experimental%20Setup)). This uses fixed model weights and in-context records, not newly trained world-model weights ([§2.2–2.3](data/assets/813b9149789f0913c5bfb94d/4e9fb103fdae9cf7e73a08394a425933da944a26fb69499d2c2935840571b3d8/text.txt#:~:text=2.2%20LLMs%20as%20Research%20World%20Models)). Preserve counterexamples: Marin selection worsens despite improved ranking, inference-selection regret favors simpler controls, and transfer-correlation intervals include zero for Marin and OLMo3-190M ([Tables 4–5 and D.1](data/assets/813b9149789f0913c5bfb94d/4e9fb103fdae9cf7e73a08394a425933da944a26fb69499d2c2935840571b3d8/text.txt#:~:text=D.1%20Uncertainty%20in%20cross-environment%20predictions)). The reported 15.8%/11.6% multi-round gains concern five evaluations selecting from pre-existing candidates with measured outcomes; they do not demonstrate unrestricted live discovery. Initial histories are outside the 24-selection budget ([E.1–E.3](data/assets/813b9149789f0913c5bfb94d/4e9fb103fdae9cf7e73a08394a425933da944a26fb69499d2c2935840571b3d8/text.txt#:~:text=E.1%20Candidate%20sampling%20and%20arrivals)). The $6.3 scoring estimate excludes acquiring the archive, reported as 171,862 H100 GPU-hours; students must assess savings against their own experiment costs ([§3.3, 'Prediction cost', and Table 1](data/assets/813b9149789f0913c5bfb94d/4e9fb103fdae9cf7e73a08394a425933da944a26fb69499d2c2935840571b3d8/text.txt#:~:text=Prediction%20cost)). Full methodological text is supplied, but artifact release remains prospective, commercial API predictions are not bitwise reproducible, and no independent replication or external researcher assessment is supplied. Authors generated the experimental records themselves; financial affiliations/conflicts are unresolved in this evidence ([Ethics and Reproducibility statements](data/assets/813b9149789f0913c5bfb94d/4e9fb103fdae9cf7e73a08394a425933da944a26fb69499d2c2935840571b3d8/text.txt#:~:text=Ethics%20statement)). Use as a qualified preprint finding and rationale for small prospective tests, not an established general efficiency gain.

Published October 7, within the September 16–October 15 UTC window. Useful new computational case study: the authors report three 24-experiment campaigns with frozen evaluation and one-hour training budgets per trial, not per campaign ([saved text, §§2–3, Table 1](data/assets/a007976d7a6dcb8c99635a7e/22bcded05aecba83c6a4594604bdc843c3061c7ccdf19d4be43c9ea27beaec4f/text.txt)). Accept as preprint evidence for bounded delegation and hardware-sensitive results, not general superiority. Only Loop B receives held-out testing; single-seed trials, model–hardware confounding, unmatched reference compute and no declared-space tuner comparison limit inference (§3.2; §4). Examine the numerical inconsistency: Table 3 gives 0.836 versus 0.833, a displayed difference of 0.003, while the prose says 0.002; do not repeat that delta as resolved. Small retained gains lack estimated run variance (§3.1). The repository is linked in the abstract, but its execution artifacts are not supplied or independently verified here. No independent replication or external researcher assessment is supplied; no conflict disclosure appears in the supplied text, so commercial interests remain unknown.
